model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; residual income equivalent on book, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total income (net interest income + non-interest income incl. net insurance income, group basis). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported; FY0 = 1H26 actual 7,998 (O39.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:63) + 2H26E ~7,950 (2Q26 4,170, 1Q26 3,828; 2H25 was 7,412). FY2025 actual 14,614. +9% on FY2025 is consistent with the 1H26 run-rate (+11%) with some fade in record trading (+46%) and insurance (+49%) income. Using FY2026E as FY0 makes year 1 = FY2027, which the engine's end-of-year discounting requires.
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,490m issued ordinary shares excluding treasury at 30 Jun 2026 (O39.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026_FS.txt:796) plus ~3m share options outstanding and ~2m DSP awards (diluted EPS equals basic, 1H26) = ~4,495m fully diluted. Held FLAT: share-plan cost (~S$64m/yr) is expensed in the flows, and the remaining S$0.8bn of the S$2.5bn capital return (buybacks + specials) is a distribution of FY2026 capital, not a falling share count in the model.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. OCBC is a MAS-regulated D-SIB: deposits of non-bank customers (S$458.9bn at 30 Jun 2026), interbank and debt issued (core_metrics total_debt S$36.7bn) are operating funding whose cost is inside net interest income; cash and central-bank balances (S$21.8bn) are held against that funding (all-currency LCR 135%). The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net profit to ordinary holders less capital retained to fund RWA growth) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE ~ distributable to ordinary holders = group net profit ~8,200 (1H26 4,195 actual + 2H26E ~4,000; 2H25 3,723) less capital retained ~3,100 to fund ~11% loan growth (CET1 transitional fell 16.9% -> 15.7% in 1H26, fully phased 15.2% -> 14.0%, i.e. FY2026 is consuming capital). Cross-check: FY2026 ordinary dividends at 50% payout ~4,100 + remaining S$0.8bn capital return = ~4,900-5,100. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based costs so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes. Informational: the engine projects from base_revenue and the driver paths.
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero: interest income is the bank's operating revenue, not a return on surplus cash.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based costs S$32m 1H26 vs S$31m 1H25 (O39.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026_FS.txt:462, cash flow add-back); FY2025 S$62m (core_metrics stock_based_comp). Awards settle from treasury shares; no net-share-settlement tax line.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buy-back of shares S$445m (kpis ShareRepurchases; 14m shares cancelled under the capital return); 1H26 S$220m (10m shares at S$20.93-22.99, O39.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026_FS.txt:800-803).
inputs.book_value_anchor: Ordinary equity S$61,648m at 30 Jun 2026 (O39.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:362; excludes S$1,698m other equity instruments and S$1,144m NCI) = NAV per share S$13.73; goodwill and intangibles S$4,348m (FS:241) -> tangible ordinary book ~S$57.3bn, ~S$12.76/share. At the current price the stock trades ~2.1x book, ~2.3x tangible book, ~15.9x FY2026E EPS (~S$1.82).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.25% SGD cost of equity, single rate across scenarios (scenario risk is carried in the flows, not charged twice in the rate). Built in SGD: 10y SGS ~2.3%, equity risk premium ~5.5%, beta ~1.0 for a D-SIB with 6.5% leverage ratio = 7.8%, +0.45pp for heavier Greater China exposure than DBS (~20% stake in Bank of Ningbo, Hong Kong CRE) and the Great Eastern insurance earnings stream with its market-linked investment gains. 25bp above the D05.SI build (8.0%) for that reason.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities (~S$254m FY2025) are inside operating expenses via the cost-income ratio; no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI (S$1,144m, mainly the ~6% of Great Eastern OCBC does not own economically, and AT1 issued by a subsidiary) is deducted through the cash_tax_rate_path, which is defined as (income tax + NCI + distributions on other equity instruments) / pre-tax profit, so the post-tax flow is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders. 1H26: (895 + 84 + ~35) / 5,174 = 19.6%; FY2025: (9,123 - 7,422 + ~70) / 9,123 = 19.4%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: residual income on book, expressed in FCFE form through the component engine, per the dcf-methods routing table row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker' and the house bank precedent (D05.SI, NAB.AX, 2016.HK) -- same structure as the D05.SI build so the two Singapore banks are directly comparable. Owner-FCF is NOT used: statutory operating cash flow swings with deposits and loans (1H26 -991, FY2024 +3,964, FY2020 +15,637). Engine field mapping: growth_rates = total income growth; ebitda_margin_path = profit before tax (after expenses, allowances, amortisation and share of associates) PLUS share-based costs, as % of total income, so the engine's SBC deduction lands exactly on PBT; da_pct_path = 0 (depreciation is inside expenses); capex_pct_path = capital retained to fund RWA growth at a constant capital ratio = NPAT margin x g / ROE; cash_tax_rate_path = tax + NCI + AT1 leakage (see nci_treatment); wacc = cost of equity; net_debt = 0. With retention = g/ROE the Gordon terminal is identically the residual-income P/B of (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) on required book. NO excess-capital equity_bridge: fully phased CET1 is 14.0% at 30 Jun 2026, exactly management's stated target operating range of 14% (O39.SI_Presentation_H1-2026.txt:724), and the remaining S$0.8bn capital return is being funded out of FY2026 earnings. Associates (~S$1.25bn/yr, mostly Bank of Ningbo) are equity-accounted and only partly paid out as dividends; treating them as distributable at the same g/ROE retention overstates near-term cash slightly, which the 25bp CoE premium partly offsets. CONSERVATISM NOT CORRECTED: FY2026 2H earnings (~S$4.0bn) are neither in the flows (year 1 = FY2027) nor in the June book; worth roughly S$0.5/share after the 50% ordinary payout and retention.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.5% diverges by >30% from revenue (7.6%), net income (15.7%) and EPS (15.3%) 5yr CAGRs. Cause: FY2020 is a COVID-trough base (ROE 7.6%, allowances S$2.0bn) and the 2022-2024 rate cycle lifted NIM from 1.54% to 2.28%, while book growth was held down by 50-60% payouts plus the S$2.5bn capital return. NIM has since given back most of the cycle (1H26 1.73%). Book CAGR is the honest compounding rate for a bank distributing most of its earnings; the base case income path (3.5-5%) sits between the two.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF is not defined for a bank; fcf CAGRs are null by design. Periods: FY2022->FY2025 (3yr), FY2020->FY2025 (5yr), Metrics.csv (shareholders_equity column = equity attributable to equity holders incl. other equity instruments).

base.growth_rationale: Total income. FY2027 +3.5%: loans +12% YoY at 1H26 (guidance raised to high-single to low-double digit) and NIM down 25bp YoY to 1.73% as Sora/Hibor fell; the rate drag fades as the deposit base reprices, but the FY2026 base is flattered by record trading (+46%) and insurance (+49%) income that will not repeat in full. 5% mid-cycle (ASEAN/Greater China nominal GDP plus wealth share gains, WM income 41% of total), tapering to 3.0% by year 10 to match the terminal rate.
base.margin_rationale: PBT + SBC on total income. Normalised PBT margin ~62.0% = 100 - cost-income ratio ~39.5% (1H26 38.5%, FY2025 40.2%, FY2024 39.7%) - allowances ~4.6% of income (~20bp on ~S$380bn of loans; guided mid-teens to low-20s bp; 1H26 S$372m) - amortisation 0.1% + associates ~7.8% (1H26 637, FY2025 ~1,200). Plus SBC 0.4%. History: FY2023 62.2%, FY2024 62.0%, FY2025 62.4%, 1H26 64.7% (record non-II); FY2018-21 53-57% at lower NIM. Drifts 40bp lower as technology/AI spend (opex +10% in 1H26) absorbs some operating leverage.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to keep fully phased CET1 at the 14% target as RWA grows with income = NPAT margin (~49.6% of income) x g / ROE on required equity 13.5% = 3.67 x g. At 5% growth 18.4% of income (37% of NPAT retained, 63% distributed -- OCBC's 50% ordinary payout plus specials/buybacks ran ~60% in FY2025); at 3% terminal growth 11.0% (22% retained). ROE 13.5% sits between FY2025 12.6% and 1H26 13.7% annualised, i.e. NIM pressure is offset by fee/insurance mix.
base.tax_rationale: Leakage rate = (income tax + NCI + AT1 distributions) / PBT: 19.4% FY2025, 19.6% 1H26, after the 15% global minimum tax took effect in 2025. 20% mature allows for top-up in low-tax jurisdictions and a larger insurance profit share to GEH minorities.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.25% CoE and 3.0% growth = 19.6x terminal FCFE, equivalent to (13.5 - 3)/(8.25 - 3) = 2.0x required book at a 13.5% ROE. Cap of 21x is a ceiling only and does not bind.

bull.growth_rationale: Rates bottom in 2026, NIM stabilises near 1.7%, loan growth holds ~10% and the wealth/insurance franchise (WM income 41% of total, record GEH contribution S$794m in 1H26) keeps non-interest income compounding double-digit under the 'Next Frontier' strategy.
bull.margin_rationale: PBT margin ~64% (1H26 run-rate 64.7%): cost-income holds ~38% via AI productivity, credit costs stay mid-teens bp, associates ~7.5%. Plus SBC 0.4%.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~51.5% x g / ROE 15% = 3.43 x g. Faster growth consumes more capital even at the higher ROE (FY2023-24 peak was 13.7% reported, ~14.5% on required equity).
bull.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.25% / 3.5% = 21.8x terminal FCFE (~2.4x required book at 15% ROE); 23x cap does not bind.

bear.growth_rationale: Sora/Hibor fall further and NIM compresses toward ~1.55% (2021 trough 1.54%); trading and insurance investment gains reverse from 1H26 records in a risk-off market; income falls 2% in FY2027 then recovers to nominal-GDP growth.
bear.margin_rationale: PBT margin ~57% = 100 - cost-income 42% (negative jaws as income stalls while tech spend continues; FY2016-21 ran 42-45%) - allowances ~35bp of loans (~8% of income; Hong Kong CRE and Greater China, cf. FY2016 726 and FY2020 2,043) - amortisation 0.1% + associates ~7%. Plus SBC 0.4%.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~45.6% x g / ROE 11.5% = 3.97 x g. ROE ~11.5% is the FY2017-19 pre-rate-cycle level. FY2027 retention floored at zero (no capital release assumed when income shrinks).
bear.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.25% / 2.5% = 17.8x terminal FCFE; the 15x cap binds deliberately (~11.7x earnings, ~1.35x required book on an 11.5% ROE), the upper half of OCBC's 2016-2021 trading range of ~1.0-1.4x book.

scenario_narratives.base: The rate headwind fades through 2027 as loan growth (~10%) and deposit repricing offset lower Sora; wealth, insurance and treasury income keep non-interest income near 40% of total, cost-income ~39.5% and credit costs at ~20bp. ROE settles ~13.5% on required equity at a 14% fully phased CET1, ~63% distributed. Worth ~2.0x required book.
scenario_narratives.bull: NIM stabilises near 1.7% from 2027, wealth AUM and GEH keep compounding, AI-driven productivity holds cost-income near 38% and credit costs stay benign. ROE ~15% with 6-7% income growth for five years.
scenario_narratives.bear: A risk-off Asia pushes NIM back to the 2021 trough, trading and insurance gains reverse, cost-income rises to 42% and Hong Kong/China credit costs reach ~35bp. ROE falls to ~11.5% and the market re-rates OCBC to its pre-2022 ~1.35x book.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 growth default, matching the house bank precedent (D05.SI, NAB.AX): OCBC is a mature, well-capitalised D-SIB whose 2023-24 ROE was lifted by a rate cycle now unwinding, so the downside (NIM + Greater China credit together) is as plausible as the upside (wealth/insurance-led fee compounding).

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding the regulatory capital its growth consumes, discounted at an SGD cost of equity -- never on statutory operating cash flow, which is deposit and loan movement, and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders is the flow; capital retained at g/ROE is the reinvestment; 8.25% is the owner's required return. This is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at ~13.5% ROE and 3% long-run growth the franchise is worth ~2.0x required book. The ~2.1x book the market pays needs ROE held near the 1H26 13.7% (record non-interest income) through a falling-rate cycle, or a cost of equity nearer 8.0%.
key_risks_to_valuation: NIM: every 10bp on ~S$520bn of average interest-earning assets is ~S$0.5bn of pre-tax income (~3% of income); 1H26 NIM was already down 25bp YoY to 1.73%, the most compressed of the three Singapore banks.
Non-interest income quality: 1H26 trading (+46%) and insurance (+49%) were records; a market reversal takes these down faster than fees.
Greater China credit and associates: Hong Kong CRE exposure and the ~20% Bank of Ningbo stake (associates ~8% of income, equity-accounted, only partly paid out in cash).
Capital: fully phased CET1 14.0% is already at the 14% target, so the S$2.5bn capital return ends in FY2026 and further specials depend on growth slowing; Basel III output-floor phase-in to 2029.
Cost of equity sensitivity: at ~2x book the value is dominated by (ROE - g)/(CoE - g); 50bp on CoE moves value ~10%.
Great Eastern overhang: failed 2025 delisting offer leaves a listed subsidiary with minorities and governance complexity.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (O39.SI, SGD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 16.74-32.57.
data_sources.financials: O39.SI_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, SGD millions) and kpis table; 1H26 performance summary and condensed interim financial statements (O39.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt, O39.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026_FS.txt) for the latest balance sheet, capital adequacy, share count and dividends; 1H26 presentation for the 14% fully phased CET1 operating target; FY2025 annual report for the S$2.5bn capital return plan.
data_sources.qualitative: Filings first; O39.SI_Analysis.json for FY2026 guidance (loan growth raised, NII to decline slightly, 50% payout, credit costs mid-teens to low-20s bp) and risk framing.
